## Decision models learn from your own examples
Astronomical's decision models (Laya, Kev and Clef) can now be fitted to your own labelled examples from the command line. Each command writes a new model folder and never changes the original:
- `astronomical decision calibrate EXAMPLES --output DIR` refits how confident the answers are, without changing which answer is picked. - `astronomical decision train EXAMPLES --output DIR` trains a decision model's final scoring layers on the graphics processor (200 labelled questions about 30 or more texts). - `astronomical decision train EXAMPLES --whole-model --output DIR` trains small add-on weights in every layer of Laya together with its final layers, so the whole model learns to read your examples differently (1,000 labelled questions about 100 or more texts; about 8 minutes for 1,200).
A result is kept only when it beats the shipped model on examples held back from training and keeps its other answers. The original files are copied unchanged, the trained parts are stored beside them, and the written model is checked against the trained one before it is used. Training shows progress with the time left, adjusts to your Mac's memory, and stops within seconds when you press Ctrl-C.
## Fixes
- Cancelling a decisions request or a training no longer restarts the engine. - Decision tools create a missing output folder's parent folders instead of refusing.
## Compatibility
Your models, conversations and settings carry over unchanged, and the configuration format is the same as 0.2.110. Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon.
This release is signed with Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and delivered as a signed Sparkle update.
